title: Extra prayers
hook: You've got the five. Now meet the extras the Prophet ﷺ kept around them, and learn witr in full.

screens.text: Since Day 3 you've prayed the five. At the masjid you've probably seen people pray a few more rak'ahs on their own before or after. Today: what those are, and witr, the night prayer you started on Day 8, in full.

variant.default: **The sunnah prayers.** Besides the five, the Prophet ﷺ regularly prayed extra rak'ahs, called **sunnah** prayers. He promised a house in Paradise to whoever prays twelve a day [Muslim 728].
variant.hanafi: **The sunnah prayers.** Besides the five, the Prophet ﷺ regularly prayed extra rak'ahs, called **sunnah** prayers. He promised a house in Paradise to whoever prays twelve a day [Muslim 728]. In our school these twelve are the **emphasized sunnahs**.
hanafi_bubbles: The twelve: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib and 2 after Isha [Tirmidhi 415; Qibla 36692].
Four before Asr is a lighter extra.

bubbles: The twelve: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib and 2 after Isha [Tirmidhi 415]. {{masjid.name}} will show you its practice.

screens.prompt: Match each prayer to its sunnah rak'ahs from the twelve [Tirmidhi 415].
The Prophet ﷺ said two sunnah rak'ahs are better than this world and everything in it. Which ones?

options.feedback: Yes [Muslim 725]. If you add only one sunnah, start with these.
Not quite. Those are emphasized too, but this praise is for the 2 before Fajr [Muslim 725].
Not quite. It's the 2 before Fajr [Muslim 725]. The 4 before Asr is a lighter extra.

screens.text: **Add them slowly.** They aren't required like the five, but the Prophet ﷺ kept them. Add one, keep it, then add another.
bubbles: "Before" sunnahs start once the prayer's time has begun. And home is a lovely place for them [First Instructions].

screens.title: Praying a sunnah
screens.intro: Pray them like any prayer, quietly. Here's a 4-rak'ah sunnah.

moves.text: Once the prayer's time has begun, stand facing the qibla and intend the sunnah in your heart.
Recite al-Fatiha and a surah quietly. In a sunnah you do this in every rak'ah.
After two rak'ahs, sit for the tashahhud, then stand.
Rak'ahs 3 and 4: al-Fatiha and a surah again.
End with the salam, as in every prayer.

screens.done_text: A 2-rak'ah sunnah ends at the first sitting, like Fajr.

variant.default: **Witr in full.** Witr is the last prayer of the night, after Isha and before dawn. {{masjid.name}} will show you exactly how it prays witr: how many rak'ahs (often 1 or 3) and the du'a in it.
variant.hanafi: **Witr in full.** It's required in our school: 3 rak'ahs after Isha, before dawn, with one salam. Recite al-Fatiha and a surah in **all three**, and sit after two for the tashahhud only.
hanafi_bubbles: The third rak'ah has one new piece: a takbir and the **qunut** (a special du'a) before you bow. Watch it next.

moves.text: After Isha, stand facing the qibla and intend witr in your heart.
Pray it the way {{masjid.name}} shows you, saying what you know in each standing.
End with the salam, as in every prayer.

hanafi.title: Witr: the third rak'ah
hanafi.intro: Rak'ahs 1 and 2 are like any prayer, with al-Fatiha and a surah. Sit for the tashahhud, then stand.

moves.text: Third rak'ah: recite al-Fatiha, then a short surah.
Say *Allahu akbar*, raising your hands {men}to your ears{/men}{women}to your shoulders{/women}.
Fold your hands again and say the **qunut** quietly.
End with the salam. Witr is done.

items: Pray the 2 sunnah rak'ahs after Isha
Pray witr, the last prayer of the night
Dawn comes: witr's time has ended
screens.feedback: That's it. Witr comes after Isha and before dawn, so it closes your night.

hanafi.prompt: Put the third rak'ah of witr in order.
items: Say Allahu akbar, raising your hands
Fold your hands and say the qunut quietly
Prostrate twice, sit for the last tashahhud, and end with the salam
hanafi.feedback: That's it. The only new piece is the takbir and the qunut before you bow.

screens.translit: Allahumma inna nasta'inuka wa nastaghfiruka, wa nu'minu bika wa natawakkalu 'alayka, wa nuthni 'alaykal-khayra kullahu, wa nashkuruka wa la nakfuruka, wa nakhla'u wa natruku man yafjuruk. Allahumma iyyaka na'budu, wa laka nusalli wa nasjudu, wa ilayka nas'a wa nahfidu, wa narju rahmataka wa nakhsha 'adhabaka, inna 'adhabaka bil-kuffari mulhiq.
screens.meaning: O Allah, we ask You for help and Your forgiveness. We believe in You and rely on You. We praise You with all good, we thank You and are not ungrateful, and we turn away from whoever defies You. O Allah, You alone we worship; to You we pray and bow down; to You we hurry and serve. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment. Your punishment will reach those who reject You.
screens.when: In the third rak'ah of witr, after the takbir, before bowing. Learn it in two halves: the first "Allahumma" this week, the second next week.

screens.text: **Still learning the qunut? That's fine.** Any du'a fulfills it, though the full one is better [SeekersGuidance, qunut]. Until you know it, say *Rabbana atina…* (from Day 30) [Q 2:201], or *Allahumma-ghfir li* three times, as on Day 8.
bubbles: Forgot the qunut and already bowed? Keep going, and do **sujud al-sahw** (the forgetfulness prostration, Day 26) at the end.

screens.text: Twelve sunnah rak'ahs a day are a gift, so add them one at a time. Witr closes the night: pray it the way {{masjid.name}} shows you.

hanafi.text: Twelve sunnah rak'ahs a day are a gift, so add them one at a time. Witr: 3 rak'ahs, and in the third, the takbir and the qunut before bowing.

screens.text: Extras grow out of a steady five, not the other way round. One more rak'ah, kept, beats ten that burn out.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Twelve daily sunnah rak'ahs earn a house in Paradise [Muslim 728]: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha [Tirmidhi 415, sahih per al-Albani]. Hanafi: these are sunnah mu'akkadah; 4 (or 2) before Asr, 2 or 4 before Isha, 4 after Isha and extra after Dhuhr and Maghrib are recommended but not emphasized [Qibla 36692 (Shaykh Faraz Rabbani); First Instructions on Worship sunna table]. Other schools generally count 2 before Dhuhr.
- The 2 before Fajr are better than the world and all it contains [Muslim 725].
- "Before" sunnahs can't be prayed until the prayer's time has begun; praying sunnahs at home is recommended [First Instructions].
- Hanafi witr: wajib; 3 rak'ahs with one salam; al-Fatiha and a surah in every rak'ah; middle sitting with tashahhud only; in the third, after the surah, takbir with raised hands, then the qunut, then ruku'. One rak'ah alone isn't valid. Time: after Isha until true dawn [First Instructions; SeekersGuidance, hadiths on witr; Qibla 36911]. `Q18`
- The qunut is wajib in Hanafi witr; any du'a fulfills it; the sunnah wording (*Allahumma inna nasta'inuka…*) is far better. Someone who doesn't know it may say *Allahumma-ghfir li* or *Ya Rabb* three times, or *Rabbana atina…* [SeekersGuidance, qunut if you don't know it; Q 2:201]. Forgetting the qunut and going into ruku': continue and do sujud al-sahw.
- Other schools commonly use *Allahumma-hdini fiman hadayt…*, which the Prophet ﷺ taught al-Hasan for witr [Abu Dawud 1425, sahih per al-Albani].

**Likely questions**
- *"Are sunnahs required?"* Not like the five. In the Hanafi school the twelve are strongly emphasized and scholars urge making them a habit; encourage adding one at a time. Don't say they're "optional, skip them," and don't present missing them as like missing a fard prayer. (scholar question Q28)
- *"I fell asleep before witr."* Hanafi: it's made up (qada) like other missed required prayers. Advise praying it before sleeping if they often miss it.
- *"Do I pray witr behind the imam in Ramadan?"* Yes, in Ramadan it's prayed in congregation after tarawih; the imam leads, they follow.
- *"Do I pray sunnahs at the masjid?"* Yes, if there's time, individually; or at home. For Fajr sunnah when the congregation has started: route to the imam (details differ).
- *"Can I read the qunut from my phone during witr?"* No card or phone in prayer (Spec §7). Use the short du'a until memorized.

**Escalate:** making up years of missed witr or sunnahs; Jumu'ah sunnahs and tarawih details (masjid practice); anyone overloading on extras and burning out (Day 8, Day 45 tone).

**Don't**
- Don't make extras feel like a new burden or a test of sincerity.
- Don't teach one-rak'ah witr as the masjid default.
- Don't recite or display the qunut's Arabic from memory; use the approved audio and text.
madhabNote: Witr is required (wajib) in the Hanafi school and a strongly emphasized sunnah in the Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, which usually pray it as 2 + 1 (with a salam between) or as a single rak'ah. Many who say a qunut in witr use *Allahumma-hdini fiman hadayt* [Abu Dawud 1425]; when and whether it's said differs by school. Other schools count 2 sunnah rak'ahs before Dhuhr where the Hanafis count 4. All are valid; follow your masjid.
